<reason>PRO better handled the central uncertainty clash: semi-automation can flag inconclusive margins and quantify error, while human calls hide unmeasured error. CON persuasively exposed plausible system errors that physical-plausibility override may miss, but did not show human-primary officiating is more accurate or accountable overall, especially after conceding technology's value as an input.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 answer on the 2mm case was decisive: treating sub-uncertainty margins as inconclusive with a no-offside default turned CON's false-precision attack into an argument for explicit machine error bars over unquantified human guessing.</best_rebuttal>
